title: Reduced scheme maps with one-point image factor through the residue field
statement: Let $Y$ and $X$ be schemes [def-pc-scheme], with $Y$ reduced [def-pc-reduced-scheme]. Let $f:Y\to X$ be a morphism and $x\in X$ a point such that $f(|Y|)\subseteq\{x\}$. Write $\kappa(x)$ for the residue field [def-weil-residue-field] and $i_x:\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)\to X$ for the canonical residue-field morphism [lem-weil-pbc-morphism-from-spec-field, def-weil-affine-spectrum]. There exists a morphism $h:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ with $i_x\circ h=f$. The scheme $Y$ may be empty or non-quasi-compact, and no Noetherian hypothesis is imposed.

proof.text: Choose an affine open $U=\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq X$ containing $x$. Since $f^{-1}(U)=Y$, restriction of the sheaf map of $f$ gives a morphism $f_U:Y\to U$ whose composite with $U\hookrightarrow X$ is $f$: on each open $W\subseteq U$ use the original map $\mathcal O_X(W)\to\mathcal O_Y(f^{-1}W)$, with its original local stalk maps. Let $\mathfrak p\subset A$ correspond to $x$. The affine-open stalk identification gives $\mathcal O_{X,x}\cong A_{\mathfrak p}$, compatible with germs, and hence $\kappa(x)\cong A_{\mathfrak p}/\mathfrak pA_{\mathfrak p}$. Choose an arbitrary affine open covering $Y=\bigcup_iV_i$, $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$. Reducedness makes every $B_i$ reduced. Write $\varphi_i:A\to B_i$ for the map induced by $f_U|_{V_i}$. No finite subcover is chosen.

source.place: Tag 0H1M (lemma-factor-through-point), affine-local hint; details supplied by Q131.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and $a\in\mathfrak p$. The germ $a_x$ belongs to the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{X,x}\cong A_{\mathfrak p}$. For every $v\in V_i$ we have $f(v)=x$, so the local stalk map of $f$ sends $a_x$ into the maximal ideal of $\mathcal O_{Y,v}$. Compatibility with germs says that this is the germ of $\varphi_i(a)$; consequently $\varphi_i(a)$ has zero value in $\kappa(v)$ for every $v\in V_i$. The affine scheme $V_i$ is quasi-compact, so the cited vanishing-section lemma makes $\varphi_i(a)$ nilpotent. Since $B_i$ is reduced, $\varphi_i(a)=0$. Thus $\mathfrak p\subseteq\ker\varphi_i$. Quasi-compactness is used only for this individual affine open, not for $Y$.

source.place: Tag 0H1M (lemma-factor-through-point), affine-local hint; details supplied by Q131.

proof.text: For $s\in A\setminus\mathfrak p$, its germ $s_x$ is a unit by the affine-open stalk localization. Ring homomorphisms send units to units, so the germ of $\varphi_i(s)$ is a unit at every $v\in V_i$. At the point of $V_i=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$ corresponding to a prime $\mathfrak q$, its germ lies outside the maximal ideal precisely when $\varphi_i(s)\notin\mathfrak q$, by the same stalk identification. Hence $D(\varphi_i(s))=\operatorname{Spec}B_i$. Clause (ii) of the cited basic-open criterion implies that $\varphi_i(s)$ is a unit of $B_i$. This argument also applies to the zero ring: its spectrum is empty and its sole element is a unit.

source.place: Tag 0H1M (lemma-factor-through-point), affine-local hint; details supplied by Q131.

proof.text: By clause (d) of the prime-residue-field algebra lemma, steps 2 and 3 supply a ring map $\lambda_i:\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to B_i$ with $\lambda_i\circ\pi=\varphi_i$, where $\pi:A\to A_{\mathfrak p}\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$. Clause (2) of the affine residue-point lemma identifies $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ with $\kappa(x)$ and says that $i_x$ factors through $U$ as Spec of this $\pi$. Define $h_i:V_i\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ as Spec of $\lambda_i$ after that identification. The composite $i_x\circ h_i$ factors through $U$ and induces $\lambda_i\circ\pi=\varphi_i$ on $A$. Affine-spectrum duality therefore gives $i_x\circ h_i=f|_{V_i}$. This uses the algebra lemma with codomain $B_i$, which may be the zero ring; it assumes no field structure on $B_i$.

source.place: Tag 0H1M (lemma-factor-through-point), affine-local hint; details supplied by Q131.

proof.text: Cover each intersection $V_i\cap V_j$ by affine opens $W=\operatorname{Spec}C$; the intersection itself need not be affine or quasi-compact. The restrictions $h_i|_W,h_j|_W$ correspond to ring maps $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to C$. By step 4 their composites with $\pi:A\to\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ are the same map, namely the one induced by $f_U|_W$. Clause (c) of the prime-residue-field algebra lemma applies to any commutative codomain $C$ and makes these ring maps equal. Affine-spectrum duality gives $h_i|_W=h_j|_W$. The equality clause of the scheme-morphism gluing lemma on the affine covering of $V_i\cap V_j$ gives $h_i|_{V_i\cap V_j}=h_j|_{V_i\cap V_j}$.

source.place: Tag 0H1M (lemma-factor-through-point), affine-local hint; details supplied by Q131.

proof.text: The compatible $h_i$ glue to $h:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ by the scheme-morphism gluing lemma. Step 4 gives $(i_x\circ h)|_{V_i}=f|_{V_i}$ for every $i$, so the equality part of that lemma gives $i_x\circ h=f$. If $Y$ is empty, use its empty open covering: the same gluing statement gives the unique morphism to $\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(x)$ and equality of the two maps to $X$. All coverings above may be infinite, and no Noetherian hypothesis was used.

Step 1: f^{-1}U=Y, so f factors through U by restricting sheaf maps (elementary); kappa(x)=A_p/pA_p via affine-open-stalk-localization (c). Step 2: a in p goes into m_v at every v, so it vanishes on the qc affine V_i, is nilpotent by the qc vanishing lemma, and is 0 because B_i is reduced. Step 3: s not in p gives a unit at every stalk, so D(phi(s))=Spec B_i and phi(s) is a unit by clause (ii). Step 4: clause (d) with codomain B_i (the zero ring allowed) gives lambda_i, and clause (2) plus Spec full faithfulness gives i_x h_i = f|V_i. Step 5: overlaps are covered by affine W, with no affineness of V_i∩V_j assumed; clause (c) and gluing equality give h_i=h_j there. Step 6: gluing over an arbitrary or empty cover. Edge cases checked: Y empty, B_i=0, non-closed x with non-qc Y, and Spec k[e]/e^2 (shows reducedness is needed).
